en: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to me: Hammam narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Malik al-Maraghi—who is Abu Ayyub—from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When one of you fights his brother, let him avoid the face."

Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdhami narrated to us: my father narrated to me: al-Muthanna narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from al-Muthanna ibn Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said—and in the hadith of Ibn Hatim from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "When one of you fights his brother, let him avoid the face, for indeed Allah created Adam in His image."

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah: he heard Abu Ayyub narrating from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When one of you fights his brother, let him not strike the face."

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "When one of you fights his brother, let him avoid the face."
'Amr al-Naqid and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, they said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, with this chain of transmission, and he said: "When one of you strikes..."

'Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us: al-Mughirah—meaning al-Hizami—narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When one of you fights his brother, let him avoid the face."
Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated to us: Bahz narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us, with this chain of transmission, the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When Allah fashioned Adam in Paradise, He left him as long as Allah willed to leave him. So Iblis began walking around him, looking at what he was. When he saw that he was hollow, he knew that he was created a creation that cannot control itself."
And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from al-A'mash, with this chain of transmission.

Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdhami narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us: I heard al-A'mash say: I heard 'Adi ibn Thabit say: Sulayman ibn Surad narrated to us, saying: Two men reviled each other in the presence of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and one of them began to get angry and his face turned red. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) looked at him and said: "Indeed, I know a word which, if he were to say it, this would leave him: 'I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.'" Then a man from among those who heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) stood up and went to the man and said: "Do you know what the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said just now? He said: 'Indeed, I know a word which, if he were to say it, this would leave him: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.'" So the man said to him: "Do you see me as mad?"

Yahya ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us—Yahya said: "informed us," and Ibn al-'Ala' said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from Sulayman ibn Surad, who said: Two men reviled each other in the presence of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and one of them's eyes turned red and his jugular veins swelled. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, I know a word which, if he were to say it, that which he feels would leave him: 'I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.'" So the man said: "Do you perceive any madness in me?" Ibn al-'Ala' said: So he said: "Do you perceive..." and did not mention "the man."

And Muhammad ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd both narrated it to us from 'Abd al-Razzaq: Ma'mar informed us; (H) and 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bahram narrated to us: Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu'ayb informed us—both from al-Zuhri, from Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

Hajib ibn al-Walid narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Harb narrated to us, from al-Zubaydi, from al-Zuhri: Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "The strong one is not the one who overcomes people in wrestling." They said: "Then which one is the strong one, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The one who controls himself at the time of anger."

Yahya ibn Yahya and 'Abd al-A'la ibn Hammad narrated to us, they both said: I read to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The strong one is not the one who overcomes people in wrestling; rather, the strong one is the one who controls himself at the time of anger."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, they said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: 'Isa ibn Yunus informed us—both from al-A'mash, with this chain of transmission, the like of its meaning.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us—and the wording is Qutaybah's—they said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from al-Harith ibn Suwayd, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whom do you count as al-raqub among you?" He said: We said: "The one to whom no child is born." He said: "That is not al-raqub; rather, it is the person who has not preceded any of his children (i.e., none of his children died before him)." He said: "And whom do you count as al-sura'ah (the strong wrestler) among you?" He said: We said: "The one whom men cannot throw down." He said: "It is not that; rather, it is the one who controls himself at the time of anger."

Minjab ibn al-Harith al-Tamimi narrated to us: Ibn Mushir informed us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated to us: 'Isa ibn Yunus informed us—both from al-A'mash, with this chain of transmission. And in the hadith of 'Isa he did not mention: "and strives for truthfulness, and strives for falsehood." And in the hadith of Ibn Mushir: "until Allah writes him down..."

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah and Waki' narrated to us, they said: al-A'mash narrated to us; (H) and Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Shaqiq, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Adhere to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man continues to tell the truth and strive for truthfulness until he is written with Allah as a truthful person (siddiq). And beware of falsehood, for falsehood leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. A man continues to tell lies and strive for falsehood until he is written with Allah as a liar."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, they said: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, truthfulness is righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise; and a servant continues to strive for truthfulness until he is written with Allah as a truthful person. And indeed, falsehood is wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire; and a servant continues to strive for falsehood until he is written as a liar." Ibn Abi Shaybah said in his narration: from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).

Zuhayr ibn Harb, 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—Ishaq said: "informed us," and the other two said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise; and a man will continue to tell the truth until he is written as a truthful person. And indeed, falsehood leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire; and a man will continue to tell lies until he is written as a liar."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: I heard Abu Ishaq narrating from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: Indeed, Muhammad (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Shall I not inform you what al-'adh (calumny) is? It is tale-bearing (namimah), the malicious gossip circulated among people." And Muhammad (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "A man tells the truth until he is written as a truthful person, and he tells lies until he is written as a liar."

And 'Amr al-Naqid narrated it to us: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, with this chain of transmission up to his words: "and convey good," and he did not mention what followed it.

'Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Salih: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn 'Ubaydillah ibn 'Abdillah ibn Shihab narrated to us, with this chain of transmission, the like of it, except that in the hadith of Salih: "And she said: And I did not hear him grant a concession regarding anything of what people say except in three things"—similar to what Yunus made part of the statement of Ibn Shihab.

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab: Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf informed me that his mother, Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt—and she was among the early emigrant women who gave allegiance to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—informed him that she heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "The liar is not the one who reconciles between people, saying good or conveying good." Ibn Shihab said: And I have not heard that concession was given regarding anything of what people say as lies except in three cases: war, reconciling between people, and the talk of a man to his wife and the talk of a woman to her husband.

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us: Shu'bah narrated to us: Abu Hamzah informed us: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: I was playing with the boys when the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came, so I hid from him... and he mentioned the like of it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-'Anazi narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—they said: Umayyah ibn Khalid narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah al-Qassab, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: I was playing with the boys when the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came, so I hid behind a door—he said: so he came and tapped me gently between my shoulders, and said: "Go and call Mu'awiyah for me." He said: So I came and said: "He is eating." He said: Then he said to me: "Go and call Mu'awiyah for me." He said: So I came and said: "He is eating." Thereupon he said: "May Allah not fill his belly!" Ibn al-Muthanna said: I said to Umayyah: "What does hata'ani mean?" He said: "He gave me a gentle pat behind the neck."

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Abu Ma'n al-Raqashi narrated to me—and the wording is Zuhayr's—they said: 'Umar ibn Yunus narrated to us: 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar narrated to us: Ishaq ibn Abi Talhah narrated to us: Anas ibn Malik narrated to me, saying: There was an orphan girl living with Umm Sulaym—and she was the mother of Anas. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saw the orphan girl and said: "Is it you? You have grown big; may you not grow old in age!" The orphan girl returned to Umm Sulaym weeping. Umm Sulaym said: "What is the matter with you, my little girl?" The girl said: "The Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) has invoked against me that my age should not advance, so now my age will never advance—or she said: my horn (generation)!" So Umm Sulaym rushed out wrapping her headscarf until she met the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to her: "What is the matter with you, O Umm Sulaym?" She said: "O Prophet of Allah, did you invoke against my orphan girl?" He said: "And what is that, O Umm Sulaym?" She said: "She claims that you prayed that her age should not advance and that her horn should not grow." He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) laughed and then said: "O Umm Sulaym, do you not know of my covenant with my Lord? I made a condition with my Lord and said: 'I am only a human being; I am pleased as humans are pleased and I become angry as humans become angry. So whomever of my Ummah I invoke against with an invocation which he does not deserve, make it for him a purification, a cleansing, and a source of nearness by which You bring him close to You on the Day of Resurrection.'" And Abu Ma'n said: "yutayyimah" (little orphan girl) in the diminutive in the three places of the hadith.

Harun ibn 'Abdillah and Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to me, they said: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdillah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "I am only a human being, and indeed I have made a condition with my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, that whatever servant among the Muslims I revile or curse, let that be for him a purification and a reward." Ibn Abi Khalaf narrated it to me: Rawh narrated to us; (H) and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated it to us: Abu 'Asim narrated to us—all of them from Ibn Jurayj, with this chain of transmission, the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, they said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: 'Isa ibn Yunus informed us—both from al-A'mash, with the chain of transmission of 'Abdullah ibn Numayr, the like of his hadith, except that in the hadith of 'Isa he made: "and a reward" in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, and he made: "and a mercy" in the hadith of Jabir.

And Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it, except that in it is: "a purification and a reward."
